condition_specific: exposure-related cancer — cancer caused by a known carcinogen to which an individual is at risk for occupational exposure (as recognized by IARC or NIOSH)
filing_deadline_notes: Former employee must have terminated employment not more than 60 months (5 years) before diagnosis; individual must be either actively employed or have terminated not more than 60 months earlier at time of diagnosis.
notes: NOTE: Indiana's WC system (IC 22-3-7-2) explicitly excludes municipal firefighters and police officers who are members of pension funds. These benefits are pension disability presumptions only, not workers' compensation presumptions. Applies to full-time employees of state or political subdivision. Tobacco exclusion: chapter does not apply to any individual who used tobacco products in any form in the 5 years before diagnosis. At time of diagnosis: must be actively employed OR have terminated employment not more than 60 months earlier. Presumption is rebuttable by competent evidence.

condition_specific: mental illness / mental health disability (including PTSD)
notes: Indiana's workers' compensation system (IC 22-3-7-2) explicitly excludes municipal firefighters and police officers who are members of pension funds -- so these benefits are pension disability provisions, not workers' compensation presumptions. This applies to 1977 Fund members (firefighters under IC 36-8-8). Mental health disability is treated as a Class 1 impairment, the same as occupational disease. The review process works like this: an initial 2-year provisional period requiring active treatment, a panel reevaluation at the end of that period, a second 2-year provisional period if the firefighter is still impaired, and permanent disability status if impairment continues after the second evaluation. This applies to final determinations made after December 31, 2012, and the employer pays for mental health care during both provisional periods. Importantly, this is a claims-administration and review-panel procedure for an existing mental-health disability pathway -- it does not create or reflect any presumption that a mental-health condition, including PTSD, is duty-related. Indiana has no PTSD or mental-health presumption of any kind.

condition_specific: mental illness / mental health disability (including PTSD)
notes: Indiana's workers' compensation system (IC 22-3-7-2) explicitly excludes municipal firefighters and police officers who are members of pension funds -- so these benefits are pension disability provisions, not workers' compensation presumptions. This applies to 1977 Fund members, both police officers and firefighters, under IC 36-8-8. The review panel includes an active or retired police officer or firefighter, depending on which fund member is being evaluated, and uses the same two-stage provisional-period structure described for firefighters. The employer pays for mental health care during the provisional periods. Importantly, this is a claims-administration and review-panel procedure for an existing mental-health disability pathway -- it does not create or reflect any presumption that a mental-health condition, including PTSD, is duty-related. Indiana has no PTSD or mental-health presumption of any kind.

condition_specific: exposure-related Parkinson's disease — caused by a toxin or head trauma known to increase risk for Parkinson's disease
filing_deadline_notes: Must be actively employed or have terminated not more than 60 months before diagnosis.
notes: NOTE: Indiana's WC system (IC 22-3-7-2) explicitly excludes municipal firefighters and police officers who are members of pension funds. These benefits are pension disability presumptions only, not workers' compensation presumptions. Parkinson's disease explicitly added as a presumptive condition (IC 5-10-15-5.5 added by P.L.59-2009). Must be caused by toxin or head trauma known to increase Parkinson's risk AND to which individual is at risk for occupational exposure. Tobacco exclusion applies. Rebuttable by competent evidence.
